symptoms: Uniform bright green colour across entire leaf
No spots, patches, rust marks or discolouration
Smooth leaf surface with no powdery coating
Strong leaf veins with no yellowing at margins
Disease Free leaves.silkworm_impact: SAFE — Healthy leaves provide full nutritional value. Silkworms fed on healthy leaves show better growth, higher cocoon weight, and stronger silk thread quality.
immediate_actions: Continue feeding these leaves to silkworms — fully safe
Harvest in early morning (6–8 AM) when leaf moisture is optimal
Store harvested leaves in cool damp cloth to retain freshness
Use within 4–6 hours of harvest for best results
prevention: Inspect leaves every 2–3 days to catch early disease signs
Maintain proper plant spacing (90cm × 90cm) for airflow
Avoid overhead irrigation — water at base of plants only

Leaf Rust.cause: Fungal pathogen: Cerotelium fici. Spreads through wind-borne spores in warm, humid conditions.
symptoms: Reddish-brown pinhead spots on underside of mature leaves
Yellow patches corresponding to spots on upper surface
Rusty powder rubs off onto fingers when touched
Premature leaf drying, curling, and early leaf drop
Leaf Rust.silkworm_impact: UNSAFE FOR FEEDING — Rust-infected leaves lose moisture rapidly, contain low protein content, and cause nutritional stress and flacherie disease in silkworms.
Leaf Rust.frequency: Spray twice at 14-day intervals (Safety period: 10 days before feeding)
immediate_actions: DO NOT feed rusted leaves to silkworms immediately
Pluck affected bottom leaves and burn or bury them outside the farm
Reduce shade around mulberry field to increase sunlight exposure
Improve drainage to prevent high atmospheric humidity around leaves
prevention: Prune mulberry bushes twice a year (after bottom pruning)
Maintain 90cm x 90cm spacing to prevent dense overlapping canopy
Avoid excess nitrogenous fertilisers which promote soft tender leaves
Spray 0.2% Carbendazim as a preventive spray before onset of winter/monsoon

Leaf Spot.cause: Fungal pathogen: Cercospora moricola. Thrives in high humidity (>80%) and high rainfall periods.
symptoms: Dark brown circular or irregular spots with pale gray centers
Shot-hole appearance where dead center tissue drops out
Yellow halo surrounding brown spots on upper leaf surface
Leaves turn yellow and dry up prematurely
Leaf Spot.silkworm_impact: HIGHLY UNSAFE FOR FEEDING — Causes severe indigestibility, intestinal blockage, and stunted growth in silkworms due to toxins produced by Cercospora.
Leaf Spot.dosage: 2g per litre of water (Mancozeb) or 1g per litre (Carbendazim)
Leaf Spot.frequency: Spray immediately; repeat after 12–15 days if spots persist (Safety period: 10 days)
immediate_actions: IMMEDIATELY isolate infected plot — do not harvest leaves from this area
Collect all fallen spotted leaves and destroy by burning
Ensure workers wash hands before touching healthy mulberry plants or rearing trays
Feed silkworms only from verified spot-free healthy sections
prevention: Collect and burn all crop residues after leaf harvest
Prune lower branches (up to 30cm from ground) to avoid soil splash
Apply recommended doses of potassium to enhance leaf resistance
Plant disease-resistant mulberry varieties (e.g., V1, G4, S36)
